prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1379; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is regarding the collision you were involved in. Do you understand that this conversation is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your current address for the record.

A: I live in Sugar Land, Texas, at the address we have on file.

Q: Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?

A: I was driving westbound on a two-lane road near a shopping center in Sugar Land. It was a clear afternoon and traffic was fairly light.

Q: What happened just before the impact?

A: A vehicle coming from the opposite direction drifted into my lane as it made a turn. I braked and steered to the right, but we still made contact head-on, though it wasn't a hard hit. I'd say we were going maybe fifteen miles an hour.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy in your vehicle?

A: No, they did not.

Q: How are you feeling since the collision?

A: I have headaches that come and go, I get dizzy when I stand up quickly, and bright lights bother my eyes. My doctor said I have a concussion and I've been told to limit screen time and rest as much as I can.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment for these symptoms?

A: Yes, I was seen at an urgent care clinic the same day and I've had two follow-up visits since then with my primary care physician.

Q: Are you currently missing any work because of your injuries?

A: I've been out for about a week and I'm working reduced hours now. My employer has been understanding about it.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get back to normal as soon as possible.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
